chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked
about the hunting of fish, and if it was not named upon it, he said: 'There is no harm with it if it is alive, that you take it.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm with it (permissible)
key_terms.لَمْ يُسَمَّ عَلَيْهِ: it was not named upon it (without reciting God's name)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish caught without saying Bismillah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the recitation of Bismillah is not a strict condition for the permissibility of fish, distinguishing them from land animals which require slaughter. The ruling specifies that the fish must be alive when captured, reflecting the Shia juristic view that fish do not require ritual slaughter (dhabihah) but rather simple extraction from water. This establishes a foundational principle in Shia fiqh regarding the ease of consuming aquatic life compared to terrestrial game.
